# tools


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Every factory takes `mx`, the largest number of characters one tool
result may hold, because the model in use sets that budget. Results
longer than `mx` are clipped with the helpers in `shalya.core`.

A tool must never raise, since an exception would end the agent’s turn.
[`resolved`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#resolved)
checks a path against the host and returns `(path, '')`, or
`(None, error)` with an `ERROR:` message the tool can return as is.
[`readable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#readable)
resolves a path a tool is only going to read, which lets a host with
`read_outside` allow reads beyond its open folders.

### readable

``` python
def readable(
    host, path, must_exist:bool=False
):
```

*Resolve `path` for reading only, which lets a host with `read_outside`
allow paths beyond its open folders.*

Every read-only tool resolves its paths through
[`readable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#readable),
so the host alone decides whether reads may go outside its folders.

## Searching the code

[`code_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#code_tools)
builds the tools for finding code. `search_code` searches the open
folders and the installed packages, by meaning when kosha’s index is
ready and literally until then. `grep` finds exact lines matching a
pattern, `ls` lists a folder, and `outline` lists the functions and
classes in one file. When the host has an index, two more appear:
`similar_code`, which finds code like the function at a given line, and
`public_api`, which lists a package’s public names.

A search can return hits the agent cannot open, for example in an
installed package outside the open folders.
[`reach_hint`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#reach_hint)
adds a line under each hit saying which tools can reach that path.
[`screen_hits`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#screen_hits)
passes hits through the host’s `read_guard`, asking once per file.

### reach_hint

``` python
def reach_hint(
    host, path
):
```

*What a model may do with a search hit at `path` on `host`: view and
edit, view only, or neither.*

The examples use a real folder and a real host. Without a kosha index,
`search_code` uses ripgrep and `outline` parses the file.

``` python
root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()/'proj'
(root/'pkg').mkdir(parents=True)
(root/'pkg'/'sizes.py').write_text('def threshold(n):\n    "Half of n."\n    return n // 2\n')
(root/'pkg'/'use.py').write_text('from .sizes import threshold\n\ndef budget(): return threshold(8192)\n')
host = LocalHost([root], index=False)
ct = {t.__name__: t for t in code_tools(host)}
sorted(ct)
```

``` python
test_eq(sorted(ct), ['grep', 'ls', 'outline', 'search_code'])          # no index: nothing similar, and no public surface, to show
assert 'threshold' in ct['search_code']('threshold')
assert 'sizes.py' in ct['ls']('pkg') and 'sizes.py' in ct['ls'](pattern='sizes', recursive=True)
assert 'sizes.py' in ct['ls']('pkg', pattern='sizes') and 'use.py' not in ct['ls']('pkg', pattern='sizes')
assert 'sizes.py' in ct['ls'](pattern='*.py', recursive=True) and 'use.py' not in ct['ls'](pattern='sizes', recursive=True)
test_eq(ct['ls'](pattern='zzz', recursive=True), 'no matching files')
assert 'recursive' in ct['ls'].__doc__
assert 'threshold' in ct['outline']('pkg/sizes.py')
hit = ct['search_code']('threshold')
assert 'view_file/replace_text' in hit and 'edit_file' not in hit, hit                # the default editor, not the opt-in one
assert 'pkg/' in ct['ls'](pattern='*.py') and 'pkg/' in ct['ls'](pattern='zzz')       # folders always show, so the model knows where to descend
test_eq(ct['ls'](pattern=root.parent.name, recursive=True), 'no matching files')     # an ancestor's name matches nothing below the root
assert 'sizes.py' in ct['ls'](pattern='pkg/*.py', recursive=True)                    # a path below the root does
```

A search covers installed packages, but the read and write tools may
refuse a path outside the open folders. Each hit’s hint names only the
tools that can reach it on this host: view and edit inside the open
folders, view only in a read-only folder or with `read_outside`, and
neither anywhere else.

``` python
from shalya.core import Hit
```

``` python
lib = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()/'site-packages'; lib.mkdir()
(lib/'sizes.py').write_text('def threshold(n): return n\n')
class Spread(LocalHost):
    def search(self, query, limit=8): return [Hit(str(root/'pkg'/'sizes.py'), 1, 'threshold'), Hit(str(lib/'sizes.py'), 1, 'threshold')]
def hints(**kw):
    "The hint under each hit, for a host built with `kw`."
    sc = {t.__name__: t for t in code_tools(Spread([root], index=False, **kw))}['search_code']
    return sc('threshold').split('\n')[2::2]   # note, then a hit line and its hint, per hit
mine, theirs = hints()
assert 'view_file/replace_text' in mine, mine
assert 'view_file' not in theirs and 'outside the open folders' in theirs, theirs     # nothing here can read it
for kw in (dict(read_outside=True), dict(read_roots=[lib])):
    mine, theirs = hints(**kw)
    assert 'view_file/replace_text' in mine and 'view_file' in theirs and 'replace_text' not in theirs, (kw, theirs)   # readable, never written
```

When a search finds nothing, the result names the engine that searched,
so the model can tell “no matches” from “the index is not ready”.

``` python
ct['search_code']('nonexistent_symbol_xyz')
```

``` python
miss = ct['search_code']('nonexistent_symbol_xyz')
assert 'no matches' in miss.lower(), miss
assert 'ripgrep' in miss or 'fallback' in miss, miss
```

The literal fallback has to work before indexing finishes. The host
below builds a real kosha index over this repository, to check search by
meaning, the public API listing, and `similar_code`. A fresh machine
spends minutes indexing the environment, so `nbdev-test` skips these
cells; `nbdev-test --flags notest` runs them.

``` python
from litesearch import repo_root
```

``` python
repo_root()
indexed_host = LocalHost([repo_root()], rerank=False)
assert indexed_host.wait_index(180), indexed_host.search_note
indexed_tools = {t.__name__: t for t in code_tools(indexed_host)}
assert {'similar_code', 'public_api'} <= set(indexed_tools), sorted(indexed_tools)   # an index makes both worth offering
sorted(indexed_tools)
```

``` python
indexed_tools['search_code']('code tools')
```

``` python
indexed_tools['public_api']('shalya.host')
```

## Files

[`file_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#file_tools)
builds the tools for reading and editing files. `view_file` shows a file
as `lineno|hash|content` lines, where the hash is a short fingerprint of
the line, and a picture comes back as an image. `replace_text` edits a
file with a list of `{oldText, newText}` pairs: each `oldText` must
match the file exactly once, and either every edit applies or none does.
`create_file` writes a whole file, and `add_root` opens another folder.
A host that cannot write gets only `view_file`.

[`exhash_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#exhash_tools)
builds `edit_file`, an editor that addresses lines by the `lineno|hash|`
prefixes `view_file` shows and refuses an edit when the line has changed
since it was viewed. It is opt-in: ask for it with
`tools_for(host, optin=('exhash',))`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L252"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### exhash_tools

``` python
def exhash_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000
):
```

*The opt-in `edit_file` tool, which edits lines addressed by the hashes
`view_file` shows.*

[`edits`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#edits) is
declared as a list in the tool’s schema, so a model sends a list. A JSON
string of the list is still accepted in this release. A string that is
not JSON, or an edit with the wrong keys, gets an error naming the shape
wanted.

``` python
ft = {t.__name__: t for t in file_tools(host)}
test_eq(sorted(ft), ['add_root', 'create_file', 'replace_text', 'view_file'])
p = root/'pkg'/'greet.py'; p.write_text('def greet(name):\n    return "hello " + name\n')
out = ft['replace_text'](str(p), [{'oldText': 'hello', 'newText': 'howdy'}])
assert out.startswith('replaced 1 block(s)') and '-    return "hello " + name' in out
test_eq(p.read_text(), 'def greet(name):\n    return "howdy " + name\n')
edits_schema = get_schema(ft['replace_text'])['input_schema']['properties']['edits']
test_eq((edits_schema['type'], edits_schema['items']), ('array', {'type': 'object'}))
assert 'oldText' in edits_schema['description'] and 'newText' in edits_schema['description'], edits_schema   # the keys are in the schema a model reads
# Review Focus 1: a JSON string still lands; a non-JSON string and wrong keys name the shape
assert ft['replace_text'](str(p), '[{"oldText": "howdy", "newText": "hey"}]').startswith('replaced')
bad = ft['replace_text'](str(p), 'oldText=hey newText=hi'); assert failed(bad) and 'list of {"oldText"' in bad, bad
assert "'oldText' and 'newText'" in ft['replace_text'](str(p), [{'old_text': 'hey', 'new_text': 'hi'}])
test_eq(p.read_text(), 'def greet(name):\n    return "hey " + name\n')
# Review Focus 2: overlap, ambiguity, emptiness, no-op: nothing is written
for es, msg in (([{'oldText': 'name', 'newText': 'who'}], 'matches 2 places'),
                ([{'oldText': 'def greet', 'newText': 'def hi'}, {'oldText': 'greet(name)', 'newText': 'hi(n)'}], 'overlap'),
                ([], 'no edits given'), ([{'oldText': 'hey', 'newText': 'hey'}], 'changed nothing'),
                ([{'oldText': 'nowhere', 'newText': 'x'}], 'not found')):
    r = ft['replace_text'](str(p), es); assert failed(r) and msg in r, (es, r)
test_eq(p.read_text(), 'def greet(name):\n    return "hey " + name\n')
r = ft['replace_text'](str(root/'pkg'/'new.py'), [{'oldText': 'a', 'newText': 'b'}]); assert failed(r) and 'new.py' in r and 'create_file' in r, r
print(ft['view_file'](str(p)))
```

A host’s `read_guard` sees what each read tool would send, and its
answer is what the model gets: the text, a masked version of it, or a
refusal. Search hits are checked once per file.

``` python
cp = root/'pkg'/'contact.py'; cp.write_text('owner = "ada@x.org"\n')
host.read_guard = lambda r: Refusal('Local only') if r.path.endswith('sizes.py') else r.text.replace('ada@x.org', '[EMAIL]')
assert '[EMAIL]' in ft['view_file'](str(cp)) and 'ada@x.org' not in ct['grep']('ada@x')
test_eq(ft['view_file'](str(root/'pkg'/'sizes.py')), f"ERROR: withheld: {root/'pkg'/'sizes.py'}: Local only")
host.read_guard = None
assert 'ada@x.org' in ft['view_file'](str(cp))
cp.unlink()
```

`edit_file` takes exhash commands addressed by the `lineno|hash|`
prefixes from `view_file`, and refuses a command whose address no longer
matches the file. Every write tool is marked with `@writes`, and
`WRITE_TOOLS` lists the same names for a caller that has only a name. A
host that cannot write gets no editor from either factory.

``` python
xt = {t.__name__: t for t in exhash_tools(host)}
test_eq(sorted(xt), ['edit_file'])
line2 = ft['view_file'](str(p)).splitlines()[1]
stale = xt['edit_file'](str(p), [['2|0000|', 's', 'hey', 'hi']]); assert failed(stale)
ok = xt['edit_file'](str(p), [['|'.join(line2.split('|')[:2]) + '|', 's', 'hey', 'hi']]); assert not failed(ok), ok
test_eq(p.read_text(), 'def greet(name):\n    return "hi " + name\n')
test_eq(get_schema(xt['edit_file'])['input_schema']['properties']['commands']['type'], 'array')
writers = {t.__name__ for t in file_tools(host) + exhash_tools(host) if is_write(t)}
test_eq(writers, {'edit_file', 'replace_text', 'create_file', 'add_root'}); assert writers <= WRITE_TOOLS
frozen = LocalHost([root], index=False); frozen.writes = False
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in file_tools(frozen)], ['view_file']); test_eq(exhash_tools(frozen), [])
assert 'greet' in file_tools(frozen)[0](str(p))   # reading still works
assert 'lineno|hash|' in get_schema(xt['edit_file'])['input_schema']['properties']['commands']['description']
```

## Notebooks

[`notebook_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#notebook_tools)
builds the notebook tools, which address cells by id, never by line.
`notebook_cells` lists a notebook’s cells with their ids, `view_cell`
shows one cell’s source with line numbers, `edit_cell` edits a cell with
the same `{oldText, newText}` pairs as `replace_text`, and `add_cell`
inserts a new cell.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L328"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### notebook_tools

``` python
def notebook_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000
):
```

*Tools to list, read, edit and add notebook cells, addressed by cell
id.*

``` python
# every write consults the host's optional guard
class Guarded(Host):
    group = 'file'
    def __init__(self): self.seen = []
    @property
    def roots(self): return ['/proj']
    def check(self, path, must_exist=False, reading=False): return Path('/proj')/path
    def check_write(self, p): self.seen.append(str(p)); raise HostError('generated')
    def walk(self): return []
    def read(self, path): return 'x = 1\n'
    def write(self, path, text): raise AssertionError(f'the guard was bypassed for {path}')
    def text_at(self, path): return ''
g = Guarded()
guarded = {t.__name__: t for t in file_tools(g) + exhash_tools(g) + notebook_tools(g)}
for nm, args in (('replace_text', ('a.py', [{'oldText': 'x = 1', 'newText': 'x = 2'}])), ('edit_file', ('a.py', [['1|ab|', 'd']])),
                 ('create_file', ('a.py', 'whole file')), ('add_cell', ('a.ipynb', 'y = 2')),
                 ('edit_cell', ('a.ipynb', 'c1', [{'oldText': 'x', 'newText': 'y'}]))):
    assert failed(guarded[nm](*args)), f'{nm} wrote past the guard'
test_eq(len(g.seen), 5)
```

A unique prefix of an id also addresses a cell, and an id that matches
nothing gets an error listing the ids.

``` python
nt = {t.__name__: t for t in notebook_tools(host)}
test_eq(sorted(nt), ['add_cell', 'edit_cell', 'notebook_cells', 'view_cell'])
said = nt['add_cell']('nb/demo.ipynb', 'x = 1\ny = x + 1'); cid = said.split()[2]
assert cid in nt['notebook_cells']('nb/demo.ipynb')
print(nt['view_cell']('nb/demo.ipynb', cid))
```

``` python
test_eq(nt['view_cell']('nb/demo.ipynb', cid), '1: x = 1\n2: y = x + 1')
out = nt['edit_cell']('nb/demo.ipynb', cid, [{'oldText': 'x = 1', 'newText': 'x = 2'}])
assert out.startswith(f'replaced 1 block(s) in cell {cid}') and '+x = 2' in out, out
test_eq(nt['view_cell']('nb/demo.ipynb', cid[:4]), '1: x = 2\n2: y = x + 1')             # a unique prefix addresses too
test_eq(host.nb_cells('nb/demo.ipynb')[0][2], 'x = 2\ny = x + 1')
r = nt['edit_cell']('nb/demo.ipynb', cid, [{'oldText': 'x', 'newText': 'z'}]); assert failed(r) and 'matches 2 places' in r
r = nt['edit_cell']('nb/demo.ipynb', 'nope', [{'oldText': 'x = 2', 'newText': 'x = 3'}]); assert failed(r) and cid in r and 'demo.ipynb' in r, r  # names the notebook and lists the ids
assert failed(nt['view_cell']('nb/demo.ipynb', 'nope'))
assert nt['edit_cell']('nb/demo.ipynb', cid, '[{"oldText": "x = 2", "newText": "x = 3"}]').startswith('replaced')   # a JSON string still lands
test_eq(host.nb_cells('nb/demo.ipynb')[0][2], 'x = 3\ny = x + 1')
edits_schema = get_schema(nt['edit_cell'])['input_schema']['properties']['edits']
test_eq(edits_schema['type'], 'array'); assert 'oldText' in edits_schema['description'], edits_schema
assert 'exhash' not in (nt['edit_cell'].__doc__ + nt['view_cell'].__doc__)
```

## The web, and what was read before

The web tools and the memory tools are separate groups, and the
difference matters.
[`web_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#web_tools)
goes to the network now: `web_search` returns titles and URLs, and
`read_url` reads one page as text and asks the host to keep it in memory
unless `remember=False`. The memory tools recall what earlier reads
found, without going out again.
[`research_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#research_tools)
adds the opt-in `research` tool, which reads the top results for a query
into one cited digest and is much slower than a search.
[`browser_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#browser_tools)
builds the opt-in browser tools, described at the end of this notebook.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L372"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### browser_tools

``` python
def browser_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000
):
```

*Tools to drive a browser tab: open, screenshot, read and reload a page,
and click, type or run JavaScript in it.*

These checks use a stand-in web backend, so they test the text the model
sees and the arguments passed on without touching the network. The host
notebook tests fossick itself.

``` python
class WebResults:
    research_note = 'fixture'
    def web_search(self, query, n=20):
        return [AttrDict(title='Python', url='https://python.org')] if query else []
    def read_url(self, url, remember=True):
        self.remember = remember
        return AttrDict(text='# Python', url=url)
    def research(self, query): return 'Python is a programming language.'

web_results = WebResults()
wt = {t.__name__: t for t in web_tools(web_results)}
```

``` python
test_eq(sorted(wt), ['read_url', 'web_search'])
test_eq(wt['web_search']('python'), 'Python\n  https://python.org')
test_eq(wt['web_search'](''), 'no results (fixture)')
test_eq(wt['read_url']('https://python.org', remember=False), '# Python')
test_eq(web_results.remember, False)
assert not any(is_write(t) for t in wt.values())
# the slow tool is an opt-in group over the same host, and a host without the web gets none
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in research_tools(web_results)], ['research'])
test_eq(research_tools(web_results)[0]('python'), 'Python is a programming language.')
assert has_effect(research_tools(web_results)[0]) and not is_write(research_tools(web_results)[0])
test_eq(research_tools(LocalHost([root], index=False, web=False)), [])
class Anything:
    def __getattr__(self, n): return lambda *a, **kw: None
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in research_tools(Anything())], ['research'])   # only a host that says `False` to the web is refused
```

## Memory

[`memory_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#memory_tools)
builds the tools over the host’s vault. `memory_search` searches
remembered pages and returns matching sections with their headings, age
and whether they are stale. `memory_read` browses: with no argument it
lists every document, with a document id or title it shows its headings,
and with a section id such as `doc#3` it returns that section.
`remember` files a note, and a later note with the same `key` replaces
it. `memory_forget` deletes a document, and only at the user’s request.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L482"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### lesson_text

``` python
def lesson_text(
    text, # the lesson: what to do the next time the cue fires
    cue:str='', # the shape of situation the lesson applies to
    component:str='', # the part of the harness it concerns, one of `LESSON_COMPONENTS`
    evidence:str='', # what in the conversation shows it
    confidence:str='', # one of `LESSON_CONFIDENCE`
):
```

*Format a lesson for `remember`: `text` alone, or one `field: value`
line per filled field, `lesson` first.*

An agent can use `remember` to record a lesson learned from a mistake,
with four extra fields: `cue` (the kind of situation it applies to),
`component` (the part of the harness it concerns, one of
`LESSON_COMPONENTS`), `evidence` and `confidence` (one of
`LESSON_CONFIDENCE`).
[`lesson_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#lesson_text)
formats such a note as one `field: value` line per filled field,
starting with `lesson`, so a vault titles the note by its first line.
Line breaks inside a value become spaces and empty fields are left out.
Without any of the four fields, the text is stored unchanged. An unknown
`component` or `confidence`, or extra fields with an empty `text`, raise
a `ValueError`, which `remember` returns as an `ERROR:` result.

``` python
print(lesson_text('filter on the root-relative path', cue='an empty filtered search', component='tool', confidence='high'))
```

### parse_lesson

``` python
def parse_lesson(
    text
):
```

*The fields of a lesson
[`lesson_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#lesson_text)
wrote, from a vault note or a memory-file line; None for a plain note.*

[`parse_lesson`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#parse_lesson)
reads a lesson back into its fields, whichever layout stored it. A vault
keeps
[`lesson_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#lesson_text)’s
lines. A host without a vault keeps one memory-file line,
`- [key] **title**:` and the fields joined by `|`.
[`lessons`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#lessons)
finds every lesson in a memory file or a vault note and skips plain
notes. Ramabana and Dhrona both read lessons this way.

``` python
full = dict(cue='an empty filtered search', component='tool', evidence='grep found nothing under src', confidence='high')
t = lesson_text('filter on the root-relative path', **full)
want = dict(lesson='filter on the root-relative path', **full)
test_eq(parse_lesson(t), want)                                                   # the vault's layout
test_eq(parse_lesson('- [k1] **paths**: ' + ' | '.join(t.splitlines())), want)   # a memory-file line
test_eq(parse_lesson('- plain note about paths'), None)
test_eq(parse_lesson(lesson_text('a habit', confidence='low')), dict(lesson='a habit', confidence='low'))
doc = f"# Notes\n- a plain note\n- [k1] **paths**: {' | '.join(t.splitlines())}\n\n{t}\nunrelated: line\n"
test_eq(lessons(doc), [want, want])
```

### watch_tools

``` python
def watch_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000
):
```

*Tools to set up, list and cancel watches: pages, web searches and
folders to re-check, and reminders.*

[`watch_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#watch_tools)
builds the watch tools. One `watch` tool covers every kind of watch the
vault supports: a page (`url`), a reminder (`remind`), a web search
(`search`) and a folder (`folder`), re-checked every `every`, such as
`'1d'`. `list_watches` lists them and `cancel_watch` deletes one by id.
No tool runs the watches; the harness calls the host’s `poll` for that.

[`ask_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#ask_tools)
builds `ask_memory`, which answers a question from remembered research
with citations. It is its own group because it needs a model to write
the answer, and a host can store and search pages without having one.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L576"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ask_tools

``` python
def ask_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000
):
```

*The `ask_memory` tool, which answers a question from remembered
research with citations.*

These checks use a stand-in memory backend with fixed answers, to test
JSON output, citations, watch listings, errors and the write marks. The
host notebook tests the real vault.

``` python
class MemoryResults:
    watch_actions = ('url', 'remind', 'web', 'folder')
    def memory_search(self, query, limit=8):
        if query == 'fail': raise RuntimeError('vault unavailable')
        return [{'id': 'd1', 'title': 'Kettles', 'text': 'boils at 100C', 'age': 60, 'stale': False}][:limit]
    def memory_tree(self, document=''):
        roots = [{'id': 'd1', 'title': 'Kettles'}]
        return roots if not document else [roots[0] | {'children': [{'id': 'd1#2', 'title': 'Boiling'}]}]
    def memory_read(self, node_id): return {'id': node_id, 'text': 'boils at 100C'}
    def memory_forget(self, doc_id): return doc_id == 'd1'
    def remember(self, text, title=None, tags=(), key=''):
        self.key, self.text = key, text
        return {'doc_id': 'd2', 'title': title or text, 'replaced': bool(key)}
    def watch(self, target, action='remind', every='1d', note=None, **params):
        self.watched = (target, action, every, note, params)
        return {'id': 'w1', 'kind': action, 'action': action, 'target': target, 'every': 86400, 'runs': 0}
    def watches(self, due_only=False):
        return [] if due_only else [{'id': 'w1', 'target': 'renew domain', 'kind': 'remind', 'action': 'remind',
                                     'every': 86400, 'runs': 0, 'last_status': None}]
    def unwatch(self, watch_id): return watch_id == 'w1'
    def poll(self):
        return {'ran': 1, 'checked': 1,
                'results': [{'status': 'ok', 'action': 'remind', 'target': 'renew domain'}]}
    def ask(self, question, ref=None, instruction=''):
        return {'answer': 'Water boils at 100C.', 'policy': 'redact',
                'pii': {'has_pii': question == 'who', 'identifying': {'name': 1}},
                'cited': [{'n': 1, 'breadcrumb': 'Kettles', 'node_id': 'd1'}]}

memory_results = MemoryResults()
mt = {t.__name__: t for t in memory_tools(memory_results)}
wa = {t.__name__: t for t in watch_tools(memory_results)}
at = {t.__name__: t for t in ask_tools(memory_results)}
```

``` python
test_eq(sorted(mt), ['memory_forget', 'memory_read', 'memory_search', 'remember'])
test_eq(sorted(wa), ['cancel_watch', 'list_watches', 'watch']); test_eq(sorted(at), ['ask_memory'])
assert 'boils at 100C' in mt['memory_search']('kettle')
assert '"age"' in mt['memory_search']('kettle') and '"stale"' in mt['memory_search']('kettle')   # 0.1.17 rows pass through
assert failed(mt['memory_search']('fail')) and 'vault unavailable' in mt['memory_search']('fail')
test_eq(json.loads(mt['memory_read']()), [{'id': 'd1', 'title': 'Kettles'}])                 # roots
test_eq(json.loads(mt['memory_read']('d1'))[0]['id'], 'd1')                                  # a document's tree
test_eq(json.loads(mt['memory_read']('d1#2'))['text'], 'boils at 100C')                     # a node
test_eq(mt['memory_forget']('d1'), 'forgot document'); test_eq(mt['memory_forget']('d9'), 'document was not forgotten')
test_eq(mt['remember']('fact', title='Facts', tags='one, two'), "remembered 'Facts' as d2"); test_eq(memory_results.key, '')
test_eq(memory_results.text, 'fact')                                                         # no lesson field: the text as given
mt['remember']('filter on the relative path', cue='an empty filtered search', component='tool',
               evidence='grep with path_filter\nfound nothing', confidence='high')
test_eq(dict(l.split(': ', 1) for l in memory_results.text.splitlines()),
        dict(cue='an empty filtered search', lesson='filter on the relative path', component='tool',
             evidence='grep with path_filter found nothing', confidence='high'))      # one line per field
test_eq(memory_results.text.split(': ')[0], 'lesson')                                       # a vault titles an untitled note by its first line
assert 'cue' not in lesson_text('x', cue='  ', confidence='low')                           # a blank field is not set
r = mt['remember']('  ', cue='c'); assert failed(r) and '`text`' in r
r = mt['remember']('x', component='habit'); assert failed(r) and 'rule, skill, extension, tool, memory' in r

test_eq(mt['remember']('fact', key='kettle-facts'), "remembered 'fact' as d2 (replaced)"); test_eq(memory_results.key, 'kettle-facts')
test_eq(wa['watch']('https://x.test', every='1h'), 'watching url https://x.test as w1, every 1h')
test_eq(memory_results.watched[1], 'url')
wa['watch']('renew domain', kind='remind', every='1w'); test_eq(memory_results.watched[1], 'remind')
wa['watch']('late chunking', kind='search'); test_eq(memory_results.watched[1], 'web')     # `search` is vishalakshi's `web` action
r = wa['watch']('/proj', kind='folder'); assert failed(r) and 'instructions' in r
wa['watch']('/proj', kind='folder', instructions='flag print()', pattern='*.py'); test_eq(memory_results.watched[4], dict(instructions='flag print()', pattern='*.py'))
r = wa['watch']('x', kind='youtube'); assert failed(r) and 'url, remind, search, folder' in r
memory_results.watch_actions = ('remind',); r = wa['watch']('https://x.test'); assert failed(r) and 'remind' in r
memory_results.watch_actions = ('url', 'remind', 'web', 'folder')
assert 'remind' in wa['list_watches']() and 'renew domain' in wa['list_watches']() and 'every 86400s' in wa['list_watches']()
test_eq(wa['list_watches'](due_only=True), 'nothing is being watched')
test_eq(wa['cancel_watch']('w1'), 'cancelled w1')
answer = at['ask_memory']('boiling point')
assert 'Water boils at 100C.' in answer and '[1] Kettles  (d1)' in answer and 'policy' not in answer
assert '[policy redact: withheld name' in at['ask_memory']('who')                          # the footer names the policy applied
test_eq({t.__name__ for t in mt.values() if is_write(t)}, {'memory_forget'})
test_eq({t.__name__ for t in wa.values() if is_write(t)}, {'cancel_watch'}); assert has_effect(wa['watch'])
for t in [*mt.values(), *wa.values(), *at.values()]: test_eq(len((t.__doc__ or '').strip().splitlines()), 1)
test_eq(sorted(WATCH_KINDS), ['folder', 'remind', 'search', 'url'])
test_eq(json.loads(mt['memory_read']('C# notes'))[0]['id'], 'd1')                            # a title with '#' is still a document
```

A vault host answers a search with vishalakshi’s context object, which
holds `results` and `related`, not a list. `memory_search` passes the
whole object on. Treating it as a list would leave only its key names.

``` python
class VaultShape:
    "What ramabana's `VaultHost.memory_search` returns over vishalakshi 0.1.17's `Vault.context`."
    def memory_search(self, query, limit=8):
        return AttrDict(query=query, encoder='model2vec',
                        results=[{'node_id': 'd1#0', 'doc_id': 'd1', 'breadcrumb': 'Kettles', 'text': 'boils at 100C', 'age': 60, 'stale': False}],
                        related=[{'node_id': 'd2#1', 'text': 'steam', 'age': None, 'stale': True, 'via': 'graph'}])
got = json.loads(memory_tools(VaultShape())[0]('kettle'))
test_eq(got['results'][0]['text'], 'boils at 100C')
test_eq((got['results'][0]['age'], got['results'][0]['stale']), (60, False))
test_eq(got['related'][0]['via'], 'graph')
class LShape:
    def memory_search(self, query, limit=8): return L([{'node_id': 'd1#0', 'text': 'boils'}])   # `Vault.search` answers with an `L`
test_eq(json.loads(memory_tools(LShape())[0]('kettle')), [{'node_id': 'd1#0', 'text': 'boils'}])
```

## The live session and the shell

[`session_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#session_tools)
builds the tools for the user’s live Python session. `run_python` runs
code in it and binds results to new names. `inspect_python` looks at
variables without changing them, and with no code lists them.
`restart_kernel` clears the session, and `read_terminal` reads what the
terminal has printed.

[`shell_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#shell_tools)
builds the shell tools. `run_shell` runs one command that finishes and
returns its exit code and output; a failing command’s result starts with
`ERROR:`. `run_shell_bg` starts a long-running command such as a server
and returns an id, `shell_output` reads its latest output, and
`shell_stop` ends it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L594"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

*Tools to run shell commands, in the foreground or in the background.*

`run_python` and the shell tools are write tools, so an application can
ask a person before they run. They report failures as text and never
raise.

``` python
st = {t.__name__: t for t in session_tools(host)}
sh = {t.__name__: t for t in shell_tools(host)}
st['run_python']('total = 6 * 7'), st['run_python']('total'), sh['run_shell']('echo hi')
```

``` python
import time
```

``` python
started = sh['run_shell_bg']('echo one; sleep 30')
rid = started.split()[1].rstrip(';')
time.sleep(0.5)
assert sh['shell_output'](rid).startswith('running\none'), sh['shell_output'](rid)
test_eq(sh['shell_stop'](rid), 'stopped')
assert failed(sh['shell_output']('cmd_nope'))
test_eq({t.__name__ for t in shell_tools(host) if is_write(t)}, {'run_shell', 'run_shell_bg'})
test_eq(sorted(sh), ['run_shell', 'run_shell_bg', 'shell_output', 'shell_stop'])
```

``` python
test_eq(st['run_python']('total'), '42')
assert 'total' in st['inspect_python']() and 'total' in st['inspect_python']('')   # empty code lists the variables
test_eq(st['inspect_python']('total + 1'), '43')
assert 'hi' in sh['run_shell']('echo hi')
host.note('a status line')
assert 'a status line' in st['read_terminal'](), st['read_terminal']()
assert is_write(st['run_python']) and is_write(sh['run_shell'])
assert not is_write(st['inspect_python']) and not is_write(st['read_terminal'])

assert is_write(st['restart_kernel']) and 'restart_kernel' in WRITE_TOOLS
test_eq(st['restart_kernel'](), 'the namespace is empty'); assert 'total' not in host.ns
class NoKernel:
    def list_vars(self): raise RuntimeError('no kernel')

assert failed(listed) and 'no kernel' in listed, listed                    # listing fails like any other inspection
```

## An API specification

[`api_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#api_tools)
lets an agent work with a web API from its OpenAPI specification.
`api_load` loads a specification and reports how many operations it has,
`api_ops` lists operations with their parameters, filtered and paged,
and `api_call` calls one operation with its declared parameters.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L666"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### api_tools

``` python
def api_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000
):
```

*Tools to load an OpenAPI specification, list its operations and call
one: api_load, api_ops and api_call.*

These checks use a stand-in API backend with three operations, to test
the JSON output, paging, parameter passing and errors. The host notebook
shows a real backend.

``` python
class ApiResults:
    def api_load(self, src, name=''): return {'name': name or 'petstore', 'operations': 3}
    def api_ops(self, group='', name='', match='', offset=0):
        rows = [{'name': 'listPets'}, {'name': 'getPet'}, {'name': 'createPet'}]
        if match: rows = [r for r in rows if match.lower() in r['name'].lower()]
        return rows[offset:offset + 1]
    def api_count(self, group='', name='', match=''):
        return len([n for n in ('listPets', 'getPet', 'createPet') if not match or match.lower() in n.lower()])
    def api_call(self, operation, name='', **params):
        if operation == 'fail': raise RuntimeError('service unavailable')
        return {'called': operation, 'with': params}

api_results = ApiResults()
apit = {t.__name__: t for t in api_tools(api_results)}
```

``` python
test_eq(sorted(apit), ['api_call', 'api_load', 'api_ops'])
test_eq(json.loads(apit['api_load']('spec.json')), {'name': 'petstore', 'operations': 3})
page = json.loads(apit['api_ops']())
test_eq(page['operations'], [{'name': 'listPets'}])
test_eq((page['matched'], page['showing'], page['more']), (3, '1-1', 'call again with offset=1'))
test_eq(json.loads(apit['api_ops'](match='get'))['operations'], [{'name': 'getPet'}])
test_eq(json.loads(apit['api_call']('getPet', params={'id': 7})),
        {'called': 'getPet', 'with': {'id': 7}})
assert failed(apit['api_call']('fail')) and 'service unavailable' in apit['api_call']('fail')
```

## Skills as tools

A skill is a document of instructions for one kind of task (see
`shalya.skills`). The system prompt lists only skill names and
descriptions, and
[`skill_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#skill_tools)
builds `read_skill`, which fetches a skill’s full text when the agent
needs it. `get_skills` is a function that returns the current list of
skills.
[`author_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#author_tools)
builds the opt-in `create_skill`, which writes a new project skill.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L698"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### author_tools

``` python
def author_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000

```

*The opt-in `create_skill` tool, which writes a new skill under
`.agents/skills/` in the first open folder.*

`read_skill` finds a skill by name or unique prefix, and a name that
matches nothing gets the list of available skills.

``` python
from shalya.skills import discover
```

``` python
skill_path = root/'.agents'/'skills'/'house-style'/'SKILL.md'
skill_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
skill_path.write_text(
    '---\nname: house-style\ndescription: How code is written here.\n---\n\nDense lines. Short names.\n')
skills = discover(roots=[root])
skt = {t.__name__: t for t in skill_tools(host, lambda: skills)}
skt['read_skill']('house-style')
```

``` python
from shalya.skills import MAX_SKILL_CHARS
```

``` python
test_eq(sorted(skt), ['read_skill'])
body = skt['read_skill']('house-style')
assert body.startswith('<skill name="house-style"') and 'Dense lines.' in body
test_eq(skt['read_skill']('house'), body)                 # unique prefix resolves to the same skill
assert "no skill matching 'nope'" in skt['read_skill']('nope')
assert 'house-style' in skt['read_skill']('nope')
assert not any(is_write(t) for t in skill_tools(host, lambda: skills))
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in author_tools(host)], ['create_skill']); test_eq(author_tools(frozen), [])   # writing one is an opt-in, and needs a writable host
class _Big:
    name, where = 'big', 'here'
    def text(self): return 'x' * (MAX_SKILL_CHARS - 400)
read_big = lambda mx: {t.__name__: t for t in skill_tools(host, lambda: [_Big()], mx)}['read_skill']('big')
big = read_big(MAX_SKILL_CHARS)       # a budget that holds the body gets it whole
assert big.rstrip().endswith('</skill>'), big[-80:]
small = read_big(MAX_TOOL_CHARS)      # a smaller one gets what fits, and the file holding the rest
assert len(small) <= MAX_TOOL_CHARS and 'saved to' in small, small[-200:]
```

`create_skill` writes `.agents/skills/NAME/SKILL.md` under the first
open folder, the layout
[`discover`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#discover)
reads, and refuses to overwrite a skill that already exists.

``` python
au = {t.__name__: t for t in author_tools(host)}
au['create_skill']('notebook-tests', 'when testing', 'Put the readable case in the notebook.')
```

``` python
made = root/'.agents'/'skills'/'notebook-tests'/'SKILL.md'
assert made.exists(), made
assert 'when testing' in made.read_text() and 'readable case' in made.read_text()
assert au['create_skill']('notebook-tests', 'again', 'body').startswith('refusing to overwrite')
assert 'kebab-case' in au['create_skill']('Notebook Tests', 'x', 'y')
assert is_write(au['create_skill'])
```

## Pictures

[`image_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#image_tools)
builds `generate_image`, which draws pictures through an OpenAI-shaped
image API. `route` says which: a function returning the `base_url`,
`api_key` and `model`, or a sentence saying how to set one up, which the
tool returns instead of calling anything. Without one it is
[`openai_route`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#openai_route),
OpenAI’s own API with `OPENAI_API_KEY`. An application with its own
model configuration, such as Ramabana’s `[jobs] image`, passes its own,
so an Azure OpenAI or other OpenAI-compatible deployment draws and
nothing is sent to OpenAI by name. `turn_route` gives the endpoint and
key of the turn’s own model, for when it draws itself. It picks an
endpoint in this order. With reference pictures, it uses the image edits
endpoint, so faces, style and palette are taken from them. Otherwise, if
the turn’s own model can draw (`draws_itself`) and no `model` was named,
the model draws through the Responses API and `from_reply` pulls the
pictures out of its reply. Otherwise it uses the image generation
endpoint. The constants below name the endpoints, the default model and
the limits.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L856"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def image_dest(
```

[`save_media`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#save_media)
saves a generated picture in the session’s `media` folder, numbered
after the highest number already used, so a front end can find the
result from its session. Without a session the folder is `media` in the
host’s first open folder, checked by `host.check` like any write. With
neither it raises rather than fall back to the process’s working
directory.

``` python
png = {'mime': 'image/png', 'data': b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + b'0' * 20}
saved = save_media(png, session=root/'s1', stem='generated')
saved, mime_for(saved)
```

``` python
assert saved.exists() and saved.suffix == '.png'
test_eq(saved.parent, media_dir(root/'s1'))
test_eq(saved.read_bytes(), png['data'])
test_eq(mime_for(saved), 'image/png')
test_eq(saved.name, 'generated-1.png')
test_eq(save_media(png, session=root/'s1', stem='generated').name, 'generated-2.png')
(media_dir(root/'s1')/'generated-1.png').unlink()          # a deleted file frees no number
test_eq(save_media(png, session=root/'s1', stem='generated').name, 'generated-3.png')
mroot = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()
test_eq(save_media(png, host=LocalHost([mroot], index=False)).parent, mroot/'media')   # no session: the host's open folder
test_fail(lambda: save_media(png), contains='no folder for media')                       # never the working directory
```

### image_tools

``` python
def image_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000, session:str='', draws_itself:NoneType=None, from_reply:NoneType=None, model_id:str='',
    on_media:NoneType=None,
    route:NoneType=None, # `() -> {base_url, api_key, model}` for the image endpoints, or a str saying how to set one up; `openai_route` by default
    turn_route:NoneType=None, # `() -> {base_url, api_key}` where the turn's own model is served, for it to draw itself
):
```

*The `generate_image` tool, which draws pictures with the turn’s own
model where it can and through `route`’s image endpoints otherwise.*

The image group needs a credential, not a capability.
[`image_available`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#image_available)
checks whether `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set, and without a route the tool
says what is missing and calls nothing.
[`tools_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#tools_for)
never checks; the application builds the group and passes it in as
`image`.

``` python
image_available(), api_model('gpt-image-1'), api_model('openai/gpt-image-1')
```

``` python
test_eq(image_available(), bool(os.environ.get('OPENAI_API_KEY')))
test_eq(api_model('openai/gpt-image-1'), 'gpt-image-1')   # a vendor prefix is stripped
test_eq(api_model('gpt-image-1'), 'gpt-image-1')
assert '1024x1024' in IMAGE_SIZES and 'auto' in IMAGE_SIZES
test_eq(IMAGE_MODEL, 'gpt-image-1')
assert RESPONSES_API.startswith('https://') and IMAGE_API.startswith('https://')
assert all(v.endswith('/') for v in API_VENDORS)
gen = image_tools(host)[0]
test_eq(gen.__name__, 'generate_image')
if not image_available():
    assert 'OPENAI_API_KEY' in gen('a kettle')            # it says so rather than reaching the wire
else: assert failed(gen('a kettle', size='3x3'))          # and an unknown size never gets sent
```

Reference pictures go to the edits endpoint, so a face or a style is
copied from them instead of described. `path` saves the result where the
caller asked, inside the open folders. `view_file` recognises a picture
and returns it as one, and `create_file` refuses to overwrite a picture
with text. The endpoints are replaced with fakes here, so nothing is
sent over the network.

``` python
from base64 import b64encode
```

``` python
png = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + bytes(32)
iroot = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve(); ihost = LocalHost([iroot], index=False)
(iroot/'refs').mkdir(); (iroot/'refs'/'rama.png').write_bytes(png); (iroot/'notes.txt').write_text('hi')
calls, _key, _saved = [], os.environ.get('OPENAI_API_KEY'), (post_image, _post_edit)
def _fake_edit(prompt, size, n, images, model=IMAGE_MODEL, **kw):
    calls.append(('edit', model, [i[0] for i in images], images[0][1]))
    return [{'b64_json': b64encode(png).decode()}] * n
def _fake_image(prompt, size, n, model=IMAGE_MODEL, **kw):
    calls.append(('gen', model))
    return [{'b64_json': b64encode(png).decode()}] * n
post_image, _post_edit = _fake_image, _fake_edit
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = _key or 'test'
try:
    gen = image_tools(ihost, session=iroot)[0]
    test_eq(gen('rama in exile', images=['refs/rama.png'], path='refs/rama_exile.png'), str(iroot/'refs'/'rama_exile.png'))
    test_eq((iroot/'refs'/'rama_exile.png').read_bytes(), png)
    test_eq(calls[-1], ('edit', 'gpt-image-1', ['rama.png'], png))
    assert failed(gen('x', images=['refs/missing.png']))
    assert 'not a picture' in gen('x', images=['notes.txt'])
    assert failed(gen('x', path='../outside.png'))
    test_eq(len(calls), 1)                                   # none of the refusals reached the wire
    test_eq(gen('pair', n=2, path='refs/pair.png').splitlines(), [str(iroot/'refs'/'pair.png'), str(iroot/'refs'/'pair-2.png')])
    plain = gen('no refs'); assert Path(plain).parent.name == 'media' and calls[-1][0] == 'gen', plain
    assert 'images' in get_schema(gen)['input_schema']['properties'] and 'path' in get_schema(gen)['input_schema']['properties']
    cwd, away = os.getcwd(), Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()
    os.chdir(away)                                           # no session: media goes to the host's folder, not the process's
    try: test_eq(Path(image_tools(ihost)[0]('no session')).parent, iroot/'media'); test_eq(list(away.iterdir()), [])
    finally: os.chdir(cwd)
finally:
    post_image, _post_edit = _saved
    if _key is None: os.environ.pop('OPENAI_API_KEY')
    else: os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = _key
ift = {t.__name__: t for t in file_tools(ihost)}
v = ift['view_file']('refs/rama.png')
test_eq(v.media, [str(iroot/'refs'/'rama.png')]); assert not failed(v) and 'image/png' in v and str(iroot/'refs'/'rama.png') in v, v
(iroot/'refs'/'blob.bin').write_bytes(b'\xff\xfe\x00\x01' * 8)
v = ift['view_file']('refs/blob.bin'); assert failed(v) and 'not text' in v and not getattr(v, 'media', None), v   # bytes that are not a picture
(iroot/'refs'/'named.png').write_text('not a picture at all')
assert not getattr(ift['view_file']('refs/named.png'), 'media', None)   # the bytes decide, not the name
(iroot/'.env').write_bytes(png); assert failed(ift['view_file']('.env'))   # a credential path stays refused
(out := Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()/'x.png').write_bytes(png)
assert failed(ift['view_file'](str(out)))                    # outside the roots
v = file_tools(LocalHost([iroot], index=False, read_outside=True))[0](str(out))
assert failed(v) and 'outside the open folders' in v, v      # `read_outside` reads text, not pictures
c = ift['create_file']('refs/rama.png', ''); assert failed(c) and 'not text' in c, c
test_eq((iroot/'refs'/'rama.png').read_bytes(), png)         # the picture survives
assert not failed(ift['create_file']('notes.txt', 'bye')); test_eq((iroot/'notes.txt').read_text(), 'bye')
```

With a `path`, drawing writes a file, and it is held to the same rules
as a write. The destination, and every `-2`, `-3` name derived from it
for extra pictures
([`image_targets`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#image_targets)),
is checked through the host before anything is drawn
([`image_dest`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#image_dest)):
never inside `.git`, never a credential path, never through a symlink,
and never over a file that is not already a picture.
[`image_refs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#image_refs)
checks the reference pictures: they are recognised by their bytes alone
(PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF), at most `MAX_IMAGES` of them, each at most
`MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`. When the API refuses a request, the error includes
the body it sent. The read-only version of the tool has no `path`
argument and saves only to the media folder.

``` python
import httpx
```

``` python
jpg, gif, webp = b'\xff\xd8\xff\xe0' + bytes(16), b'GIF89a' + bytes(16), b'RIFF\0\0\0\0WEBPVP8 ' + bytes(8)
test_eq([picture_mime(b) for b in (png, jpg, gif, webp, b'<svg xmlns="x"/>', b'all:\n\techo')], ['image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', None, None])
(iroot/'main.py').write_text('print(1)\n'); (iroot/'Makefile').write_text('all:\n'); (iroot/'.env').write_text('KEY=1\n')
(iroot/'fake.png').write_text('not a picture'); (iroot/'logo.svg').write_text('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>')
(iroot/'.git').mkdir(); (iroot/'.git'/'config').write_text('[core]\n')
outside = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()/'victim.txt'; outside.write_text('keep')
(iroot/'refs'/'img-2.png').symlink_to(outside)
for bad in ('Makefile', '.env', 'fake.png', 'logo.svg'): assert 'not a picture' in image_refs(ihost, [bad])[1], bad
assert 'at most' in image_refs(ihost, ['refs/rama.png'] * (MAX_IMAGES + 1))[1]
with open(iroot/'big.png', 'wb') as f: f.write(png); f.truncate(MAX_IMAGE_BYTES + 1)
assert 'over' in image_refs(ihost, ['big.png'])[1]
calls, _key, _saved = [], os.environ.get('OPENAI_API_KEY'), (post_image, _post_edit)
post_image, _post_edit = _fake_image, _fake_edit
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = _key or 'test'
try:
    gen = image_tools(ihost, session=iroot)[0]
    for dest in ('main.py', '.git/config', 'refs/img.png'):   # a text file, git's own, a planted symlink for the -2 name
        out = gen('x', n=2, path=dest); assert failed(out), (dest, out)
    test_eq((iroot/'main.py').read_text(), 'print(1)\n'); test_eq((iroot/'.git'/'config').read_text(), '[core]\n'); test_eq(outside.read_text(), 'keep')
    test_eq(calls, [])                                                       # refused before anything was drawn
    assert not failed(gen('again', path='refs/rama_exile.png'))             # over a picture is allowed
    assert 'whole number' in gen('x', n='two')
    ro = gen.read_only                                                       # what `read_only` hands a view that must not write
    test_eq(ro.__name__, 'generate_image'); assert 'path' not in get_schema(ro)['input_schema']['properties']
    assert 'images' in get_schema(ro)['input_schema']['properties'] and has_effect(ro)
    assert Path(ro('plain')).parent.name == 'media'
finally:
    post_image, _post_edit = _saved
sent, _hp = [], httpx.post
def _refuse(url, **kw):
    sent.append((url, kw))
    return httpx.Response(400, text='{"error": {"message": "Invalid value for size"}}', request=httpx.Request('POST', url))
httpx.post = _refuse
try:
    gen = image_tools(ihost, session=iroot)[0]
    assert 'Invalid value for size' in gen('x'), gen('x')
    assert 'Invalid value for size' in gen('x', images=['refs/rama.png'])
    test_eq(sent[-1][1]['data']['input_fidelity'], 'high')                   # a reference face is kept, not paraphrased
finally:
    httpx.post = _hp
    if _key is None: os.environ.pop('OPENAI_API_KEY')
    else: os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = _key
assert 'not a text file' in ift['replace_text']('refs/rama.png', [{'oldText': 'a', 'newText': 'b'}])
```

``` python
# a route of the application's own: Azure's v1 API, with its key, and nothing sent to OpenAI by name
sent, _hp = [], httpx.post
def _ok(url, **kw):
    sent.append((url, kw['headers']['Authorization'], (kw.get('json') or kw.get('data') or {}).get('model')))
    return httpx.Response(200, json={'data': [{'b64_json': b64encode(png).decode()}]}, request=httpx.Request('POST', url))
httpx.post = _ok
az = dict(base_url='https://r.openai.azure.com/openai/v1', api_key='azk', model='my-image')
try:
    gen = image_tools(ihost, session=iroot, route=lambda: az)[0]
    assert not failed(gen('a kettle')) and not failed(gen('rama', images=['refs/rama.png']))
    test_eq(sent, [('https://r.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/images/generations', 'Bearer azk', 'my-image'),
                   ('https://r.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/images/edits', 'Bearer azk', 'my-image')])
    none = image_tools(ihost, session=iroot, route=lambda: 'no image model is set up: add [jobs] image in config.toml')[0]
    assert 'add [jobs] image' in none('a kettle') and len(sent) == 2   # it says how, and calls nothing
finally: httpx.post = _hp
_k = os.environ.pop('OPENAI_API_KEY', None)
test_eq(openai_route(), 'OPENAI_API_KEY is not set')
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = 'k'; test_eq(openai_route('m'), {'base_url': OPENAI_BASE, 'api_key': 'k', 'model': 'm'})
if _k is None: os.environ.pop('OPENAI_API_KEY')
else: os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = _k
```

``` python
test_eq(image_targets('refs/rama.png', 3), ['refs/rama.png', 'refs/rama-2.png', 'refs/rama-3.png'])
test_eq(image_targets('a.png', 1), ['a.png'])
_saved = post_image, _post_edit; post_image, _post_edit = _fake_image, _fake_edit
```

The live check calls the real OpenAI image endpoint and checks that the
saved file is a non-empty picture. It is marked `eval: false` and left
out of the test run, because it spends credits.

``` python
image_root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
image_host = LocalHost([image_root], index=False)
generate_image = image_tools(image_host, session=image_root)[0]
image_result = generate_image('A simple black circle centered on a white background', n=1)
assert not image_result.startswith('ERROR:'), image_result
image_path = Path(image_result.strip())
assert image_path.exists() and image_path.stat().st_size > 1000
assert mime_for(image_path).startswith('image/')
```

## Git

[`git_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#git_tools)
builds the git tools on top of `gheasy`. The read tools are
`git_status`, `git_divergence` (how the branch differs from another,
with the outcome of a fast-forward, merge, rebase or reset worked out in
advance), `git_diff` and `git_log`. The write tools are `git_commit`,
`git_checkout`, `git_stash` and `git_remote` (fetch, pull or push).
Every tool takes `path` to choose the repository, and
[`git_repo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#git_repo)
finds it: the repository holding `path`, else the host’s project, else
its first open folder. A repository found by walking up from a path must
still lie inside the open folders.
[`screen_diff`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#screen_diff)
passes each file’s part of a diff through the host’s `read_guard`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L974"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### git_repo

``` python
def git_repo(
    host, path:str=''
):
```

*The repository holding `path`, else the host’s project, else its first
root; refused outside the open folders.*

The example uses a real repository with one commit and one untracked
file. Every write returns gheasy’s report: `result`,
[`summary`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#summary), the
`undo` token when gheasy recorded one (`''` for a stash push, a fetch, a
push or a new branch), and the repository state.

A manual check, not a test: `git_remote('push')` on a clone of an https
remote with no credential helper returns
`ERROR: git push: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled`
within a second, because building
[`git_tools`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#git_tools)
sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`. Without that, git would wait for a
password nobody can type.

``` python
repo = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()/'repo'
repo.mkdir(parents=True)
(repo/'a.py').write_text('x = 1\n')
for c in (['init', '-q', '-b', 'main'], ['config', 'user.email', 't@e'], ['config', 'user.name', 'T'],
          ['add', 'a.py'], ['commit', '-qm', 'first']):
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo)] + c, check=True)
(repo/'b.py').write_text('y = 2\n')
ghost = LocalHost([repo], index=False)
_gtp = os.environ.pop('GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT', None)   # the assertion below is about building the group, not the outer shell
git_tools(None); assert 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT' not in os.environ                # naming the tools touches nothing; a host building them does
gt = {t.__name__: t for t in git_tools(ghost)}
status = json.loads(gt['git_status']())
status['branch'], status['clean'], [c['path'] for c in status['changes']]
```

``` python
test_eq(status['branch'], 'main')
test_eq(status['clean'], False)
test_eq([c['path'] for c in status['changes']], ['b.py'])
test_eq(sorted(gt), sorted(GIT_TOOLS)); assert 'git_rebase_preview' not in gt      # divergence carries the rehearsal now
test_eq({t.__name__ for t in git_tools(ghost) if is_write(t)}, set(GIT_WRITE_TOOLS))
test_eq(os.environ.get('GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT'), '0')                                # building the group disarms credential prompts
if _gtp is not None: os.environ['GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT'] = _gtp
for t in gt.values(): test_eq(len((t.__doc__ or '').strip().splitlines()), 1)

assert failed(gt['git_divergence']()) and 'tracks nothing' in gt['git_divergence']()
test_eq(subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), 'status', '--porcelain'],
                       capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip(), '?? b.py')

assert failed(gt['git_checkout']('no-such-branch'))
assert 'op must be one of' in gt['git_remote']('nonsense')   # never reaches the network
fetched = gt['git_remote']('fetch')                          # no remote, so it is a no-op not a lie
assert failed(fetched) or json.loads(fetched)['branch'] == 'main', fetched
test_eq(sorted(status), sorted(STATE_KEYS))                                        # state only: no empty write report
```

``` python
(repo/'a.py').write_text('x = 2\n')
assert '+x = 2' in gt['git_diff']() and gt['git_diff'](staged=True) == '(no changes)'
assert '+x = 2' in gt['git_diff'](path='a.py') and gt['git_diff'](path='b.py') == '(no changes)'
# a branch with its own commit: divergence against main carries the rebase rehearsal the old preview gave
made = json.loads(gt['git_checkout']('feature', create=True))
test_eq((made['branch'], made['result']), ('feature', 'created and switched to feature'))
committed = json.loads(gt['git_commit']('second', 'a.py b.py'))
test_eq((committed['clean'], committed['moved'], committed['undoes'] != ''), (True, True, True))
assert committed['undo'] and committed['summary'], committed
div = json.loads(gt['git_divergence'](against='main'))
test_eq((div['relation'], div['ahead'], div['behind']), ('ahead', 1, 0))
assert 'stops_at' in next(o for o in div['options'] if o['op'] == 'rebase')
amended = json.loads(gt['git_commit']('second, amended', amend=True)); assert amended['undo']
test_eq([c['subject'] for c in json.loads(gt['git_log'](5))], ['second, amended', 'first'])
assert failed(gt['git_commit'](''))
(repo/'a.py').write_text('x = 3\n'); stashed = json.loads(gt['git_stash']())
test_eq((stashed['clean'], stashed['undo']), (True, ''))                    # stash push is not journaled
test_eq((repo/'a.py').read_text(), 'x = 2\n')
popped = json.loads(gt['git_stash']('pop')); test_eq((repo/'a.py').read_text(), 'x = 3\n'); assert popped['undo']
assert 'action must be one of' in gt['git_stash']('nonsense')
# Review Focus 4: a remote that is not there fails fast with an error string, never a hang
subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), 'remote', 'add', 'origin', 'file:///nonexistent/remote.git'], check=True)
pushed = gt['git_remote']('push', publish=True); assert failed(pushed), pushed
assert json.loads(gt['git_stash']('push', message='wip'))['clean']
test_eq(gt['git_checkout']('main')[:1], '{')
```

`git_commit` chooses its repository from `path` by the same
[`git_repo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#git_repo)
rule as the other git tools. Its `paths` are relative to that
repository.

``` python
other = repo.parent/'other'
other.mkdir()
for c in (['init', '-q', '-b', 'main'], ['config', 'user.email', 't@e'], ['config', 'user.name', 'T'], ['commit', '-q', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'first']):
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(other)] + c, check=True)
(other/'c.py').write_text('z = 1\n')
two = LocalHost([repo, other], index=False)
g2 = {t.__name__: t for t in git_tools(two)}
test_eq(git_repo(two, str(other)).root, other); test_eq(git_repo(two).root, repo)
heads = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
made2 = json.loads(g2['git_commit']('in the second repository', 'c.py', path=str(other)))
assert made2['undo'] and made2['clean'], made2
test_eq(subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(other), 'log', '-1', '--format=%s'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip(), 'in the second repository')
test_eq(subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(repo), 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout, heads)   # the first repository is untouched
test_eq(summarise(g2['git_commit'], {'message': 'm', 'path': 'other'}), 'Git commit: m in other')
assert 'outside the open folders' in g2['git_commit']('x', path=str(repo.parent))
```

## Which tools a host gets

`tools_for(host)` builds the tools for every group in `host.provides`,
in the order of `GROUPS`. `drop` removes groups by name. `get_skills`
adds `read_skill`. `image` is a list of already-built image tools, or
None: building them needs to know what the turn’s model can do, which
the application knows and the host does not. `optin` adds groups that
are off by default, and `extra` adds any other tools at the end.

## Tools nobody gets by default

Five groups are offered only when a caller names them in `optin`:
`exhash` (`edit_file`), `research`, `author` (`create_skill`), `browser`
(for a host that has one) and `legacy`. The legacy tools are shims for
one release, for MCP clients that still send the old names:
`list_files`, `list_vars`, `environment`, `memory_tree`, `set_reminder`,
`watch_url` and `git_rebase_preview`. Each calls its replacement, and
its docstring names it. They are removed in 0.2.0.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L1034"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### legacy_tools

``` python
def legacy_tools(
    host, mx:int=6000
):
```

*Shims, for one release, for old tool names an MCP client may still
send; each calls its replacement.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L1103"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### tools_for

``` python
def tools_for(
    host, get_skills:NoneType=None, extra:tuple=(), mx:int=6000, drop:tuple=(), image:NoneType=None, optin:tuple=()
):
```

*The tools for every group `host` provides, less `drop`, plus skills,
image tools, the `optin` groups and `extra`.*

Code without a host sometimes needs a tool’s group, for example to label
a call read back from a saved conversation, where only the tool’s name
survives.
[`tool_groups`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#tool_groups)
maps every tool name shalya can build to its group, and `group_of(name)`
looks one up. The table is built by calling every factory without a
host. A factory only defines functions that refer to the host, so this
costs nothing and calls nothing. Opt-in tools are filed under the group
they extend, so `edit_file` is in `file` and `research` in `web`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L1126"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### group_of

``` python
def group_of(
    name, default:str=''
):
```

*Which group a tool belongs to, or `default` for a name shalya does not
build.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L1115"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### tool_groups

``` python
def tool_groups():
```

*Every tool name shalya can build, mapped to its group, including the
image, skill and opt-in tools.*

`GROUPS` pairs each capability class with its factory. The group name is
written only once, on the class, and the tests check that every
capability class has a factory.

``` python
[cap.group for cap, _ in GROUPS]
```

``` python
from shalya.host import (ApiHost, AskHost, BrowserHost, CodeHost, GitHost, MemoryHost, NotebookHost,
                         SessionHost, ShellHost, WatchHost, WebHost)
```

``` python
declared = {c.group for c in (CodeHost, WebHost, BrowserHost, NotebookHost, MemoryHost, AskHost, WatchHost,
                              SessionHost, ShellHost, ApiHost, GitHost)} | {'file'}
test_eq({cap.group for cap, _ in GROUPS} | {'browser'}, declared)   # every capability has a factory; `browser`'s is the opt-in
test_eq(len(GROUPS), len(declared) - 1)                   # named once each
assert all(callable(f) for _, f in GROUPS)
```

A host over a git repository with no vault and no index gets seven
groups: code, file, notebook, web, session, shell and git, 30 tools in
all. A vault would add the memory, watch and ask groups, and an index
would add `similar_code` and `public_api`. Groups the host cannot serve
are simply absent, and nothing opt-in appears.

``` python
ts = tools_for(ghost)
sorted(t.__name__ for t in ts)
```

``` python
names = {t.__name__ for t in ts}
assert {'search_code', 'ls', 'view_file', 'replace_text', 'run_shell', 'inspect_python', 'git_status', 'git_divergence'} <= names, names
assert not (names & {'list_files', 'list_vars', 'environment', 'edit_file', 'research', 'create_skill', 'git_rebase_preview',
                     'memory_search', 'api_load', 'watch'}), 'no vault, no specs, nothing opt-in'
test_eq(len(names), 4 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 8)            # code, file, notebook, web, session, shell, git: 30 with no vault or index
test_eq(names, {t.__name__ for t in tools_for(ghost)})
```

``` python
fewer = {t.__name__ for t in tools_for(ghost, drop=['shell', 'git'])}
test_eq(names - fewer, {'run_shell', 'run_shell_bg', 'shell_output', 'shell_stop', *GIT_TOOLS})
assert 'search_code' in fewer
```

`optin` adds the groups that are off by default. Each opt-in factory
returns nothing when the host cannot back it, such as `research` without
web access, and an unknown name raises an error instead of being
ignored. Tools in `extra` still come last.

``` python
with_all = {t.__name__ for t in tools_for(ghost, optin=('exhash', 'research', 'author', 'legacy'))}
assert {'edit_file', 'research', 'create_skill', 'list_files', 'list_vars', 'environment', 'git_rebase_preview'} <= with_all, with_all
noweb = LocalHost([repo], index=False, web=False)
test_eq({t.__name__ for t in tools_for(noweb, optin=('research',))} & {'research'}, set())   # an opt-in the host cannot back is empty
test_fail(lambda: tools_for(ghost, optin=('nope',)), contains='optin')
test_eq(tools_for(ghost, optin=('exhash',))[-1].__name__, 'edit_file')
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in tools_for(ghost, optin=('exhash',), extra=[ct['grep']])][-2:], ['edit_file', 'grep'])
# a vault host stays under the budget the spec sets
vh = LocalHost([repo], index=False, memory=memory_results)       # `MemoryResults` stands in for a vault
vnames = {t.__name__ for t in tools_for(vh)}
assert {'memory_search', 'memory_read', 'remember', 'memory_forget', 'watch', 'list_watches', 'cancel_watch', 'ask_memory'} <= vnames, vnames
test_eq(len(vnames), 30 + 4 + 3 + 1); assert len(vnames) <= 45
test_eq(tools_for(ghost, optin='exhash')[-1].__name__, 'edit_file')                        # one name as a bare string
```

The legacy shims call their replacements and name them in their
docstrings. A host without a vault gets no memory or watch shims.

``` python
lg = {t.__name__: t for t in legacy_tools(ghost)}
test_eq(sorted(lg), ['environment', 'git_rebase_preview', 'list_files', 'list_vars'])
assert 'a.py' in lg['list_files']('a.py') and lg['list_files']('zzz') == 'no matching files'
assert all('use `' in (t.__doc__ or '').lower() for t in lg.values())
assert not failed(lg['list_vars']()) and not failed(lg['environment']())
assert 'relation' in json.loads(lg['git_rebase_preview']('feature'))
test_eq(sorted(t.__name__ for t in legacy_tools(vh)), ['environment', 'git_rebase_preview', 'list_files', 'list_vars', 'memory_tree', 'set_reminder', 'watch_url'])
class VaultLike:                                                                 # the host API over the fixture, declaring only the vault groups
    def can(self, group): return group in ('memory', 'watch')
    def __getattr__(self, name): return getattr(memory_results, name)
lgv = {t.__name__: t for t in legacy_tools(VaultLike())}
test_eq(sorted(lgv), ['memory_tree', 'set_reminder', 'watch_url'])
test_eq(json.loads(lgv['memory_tree']()), [{'id': 'd1', 'title': 'Kettles'}])
test_eq(lgv['set_reminder']('renew domain', every='1w'), 'watching remind renew domain as w1, every 1w'); test_eq(memory_results.watched[1], 'remind')
lgv['watch_url']('https://x.test'); test_eq(memory_results.watched[1], 'url')
assert has_effect(lgv['set_reminder']) and has_effect(lgv['watch_url']) and not any(is_write(t) for t in lgv.values())
test_eq(len(legacy_tools(None)), 7)                                              # buildable without a host, as `tool_groups` needs
```

`file` is not a capability class a host inherits. Every host has the
folder boundary, so every host gets the file tools. `GROUPS` still lists
it, so `drop=['file']` can remove them.

## What a sub-agent may have

A sub-agent that only looks things up should not change anything.
`read_only(tools)` returns the tools it may have. Every write tool is
removed, unless the tool provides a read-only version of itself in its
[`read_only`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/tools.html#read_only)
attribute, which is then used instead. `writes=True` keeps the write
tools. `block` removes tools by name. `max_calls` puts the result behind
a hard budget: once the sub-agent has made that many calls in total,
every tool answers that the budget is spent.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/shalya/blob/main/shalya/tools.py#L1136"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### read_only

``` python
def read_only(
    tools, max_calls:NoneType=None, writes:bool=False, effects:bool=True, block:tuple=()
):
```

*`tools` without write tools (or without any tool that acts, with
`effects=False`), optionally behind a budget of `max_calls` calls.*

Write tools are removed whatever else the host offers. `effects=False`
also removes the tools that act without writing a file the user owns:
inspecting the live session, an API call that may change something on a
server, drawing a picture that costs money, a watch that keeps running
after the turn, a research digest, stopping a background command, and
the browser’s looking tools. `ACTING_TOOLS` names them all. An agent
asked to propose, not act, should not have them either. `read_url`
stays, through its read-only version, which reads the page without
saving it to memory.

``` python
[t.__name__ for t in read_only(ts)]
```

``` python
ro = {t.__name__ for t in read_only(ts)}
test_eq(ro & WRITE_TOOLS, set())
assert 'search_code' in ro and 'git_status' in ro
test_eq({t.__name__ for t in read_only(ts, writes=True)} & {'create_file'}, {'create_file'})
safe_web = {t.__name__: t for t in read_only(wt.values())}
test_eq(wt['read_url'].read_only, safe_web['read_url'])
safe_web['read_url']('https://python.org')
test_eq(web_results.remember, False)
test_eq(set(get_schema(safe_web['read_url'])['input_schema']['properties']), {'url'})
full_web = {t.__name__: t for t in read_only(wt.values(), writes=True)}
full_web['read_url']('https://python.org')
test_eq(web_results.remember, True)
draw = image_tools(host)[0]                                          # a path is a write: the read-only view has none
test_eq([t for t in read_only([draw])], [draw.read_only]); test_eq(read_only([draw], writes=True), [draw])
assert 'path' not in get_schema(read_only([draw])[0])['input_schema']['properties']

# `effects=False` also withholds what acts without writing a file the user owns
acting = {t.__name__ for t in ts if has_effect(t)}
test_eq(acting - ACTING_TOOLS, set())              # nothing is marked without being named
assert acting <= ro                                # and the default keeps every one of them
propose = {t.__name__ for t in read_only(ts, effects=False)}
test_eq(propose & (WRITE_TOOLS | ACTING_TOOLS), set())
assert 'search_code' in propose                    # looking is still allowed
# Review Focus 5: what a sub-agent keeps of the opt-ins
ro_opt = {t.__name__ for t in read_only(tools_for(ghost, optin=('exhash', 'research', 'legacy')))}
assert 'research' in ro_opt and 'list_files' in ro_opt and 'edit_file' not in ro_opt, ro_opt
assert 'research' not in {t.__name__ for t in read_only(tools_for(ghost, optin=('research',)), effects=False)}
```

With a budget, the tools themselves stop the loop. A local model engine
runs its own tool loop, so a limit the harness keeps outside the tools
could not be enforced. In this example the second call is refused.

``` python
budgeted = {t.__name__: t for t in read_only(ts, max_calls=1)}
budgeted['search_code']('threshold'), budgeted['ls']('.')
```

``` python
budgeted = {t.__name__: t for t in read_only(ts, max_calls=1)}
budgeted['ls']('.')
assert 'budget exhausted' in budgeted['ls']('.'), 'the second call should have been refused'
```

## The browser

The browser group is a tab the agent drives. Looking at a page
(`browse`, `screenshot`, `page_text`, `page_reload`) acts without
writing. Acting on it (`page_click`, `page_type`, `page_eval`) counts as
a write and goes to a person. A screenshot comes back as
[`Media`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/core.html#media): text
naming the saved file, carrying the picture for an agent loop that can
send it to the model. The example uses a stand-in browser host.

``` python
class Tab(Host, BrowserHost):
    "A browser host over a dict of pages."
    roots, check, walk, read, write, text_at = (), None, None, None, None, None
    def __init__(self): self.seen = []
    def browse(self, url): self.seen.append(('browse', url)); return f'p1 Example'
    def screenshot(self, page=''): return '/tmp/p1.png'
    def page_text(self, page=''): return '# Example'
    def page_reload(self, page=''): return 'Example'
    def page_click(self, page, x, y): self.seen.append(('click', page, x, y)); return 'clicked'
    def page_type(self, page, text): return 'typed'
    def page_eval(self, page, js): raise ValueError('refused on this origin')
tab = Tab()
assert not any(group_of(t.__name__) == 'browser' for t in tools_for(tab)), 'opt-in: a host that can browse still offers nothing unasked'
bt = {t.__name__: t for t in tools_for(tab, optin=('browser',))}
test_eq(OPTIN['browser'](LocalHost([Path('.')], index=False, web=False)), [])   # named for a host without the group: nothing
test_eq([n for n in bt if group_of(n) == 'browser'], ['browse', 'screenshot', 'page_text', 'page_reload', 'page_click', 'page_type', 'page_eval'])
test_eq(bt['browse'](' https://example.com '), 'p1 Example'); test_eq(tab.seen[0], ('browse', 'https://example.com'))
s = bt['screenshot'](); test_eq(s.media, ['/tmp/p1.png']); assert '/tmp/p1.png' in s and not failed(s)
bt['page_click']('p1', '3', 4.0); test_eq(tab.seen[-1], ('click', 'p1', 3, 4))
assert failed(bt['page_eval']('p1', '1')) and 'refused' in bt['page_eval']('p1', '1')   # a host refusal is one tool failure
test_eq({n for n, t in bt.items() if group_of(n) == 'browser' and is_write(t)}, {'page_click', 'page_type', 'page_eval'})
test_eq({n for n, t in bt.items() if group_of(n) == 'browser' and has_effect(t)}, {'browse', 'screenshot', 'page_text', 'page_reload'})
assert {'page_click', 'page_type', 'page_eval'} <= WRITE_TOOLS and {'browse', 'screenshot', 'page_text', 'page_reload'} <= ACTING_TOOLS
test_eq({t.__name__ for t in read_only(bt.values())} & {'page_click', 'page_type', 'page_eval'}, set())
assert not issubclass(LocalHost, BrowserHost) and not LocalHost([Path('.')], index=False, web=False).can('browser')   # owes none of the methods
```
